Partition-in-kind vs. licitation dispute between co-owners of plantations; no letting/lodging issue.

holding_summary: Plaintiff railroad leased a building, previously used as a boarding-house and lodging-house for its drivers and employees, to defendant; when defendant opened a bar-room and gaming-house on the premises without authorization, the court enjoined that use as contrary to the destination for which the lease was intended, though it declined to dissolve the lease absent proven loss.

quotes.text: that the building leased was contiguous to the depot and stables of plaintiff at the corner of Napoleon and St. Charles aveuues, and was built to serve as a boarding-house and lodging-house for drivers and other employees; that it had been used to some extent for that purpose, and had never been otherwise used except, partially, as business offices;

Thus, not only shall the lessee, in default of an express stipulation, not be permitted to. establish, in a privaté dwelling, a house of prostitution, or a gambling house; but he cannot transform a private apartment into a restaurant, a coffee-house, a club, nor a private house into an inn or a hotel.

notes: Company-owned boarding-house/lodging-house building leased to a private lessee; dispute is over unauthorized conversion to a bar-room, not over the propriety of the underlying boarding-house/lodging use itself, hence mixed polarity and low-moderate relevance.
Ordinary multi-year (Dec. 1860-Oct. 1863) dwelling-house lease and surety liability upon lessee's abandonment; standard long-term landlord-tenant law, not short-term letting/lodging.
Sheriff's liability for hotel furniture stolen during a provisional-seizure/rent dispute; the hotel/boarding operation is incidental background, not the issue litigated.
Party-wall cost-sharing dispute between adjoining owners; a pre-existing lease is mentioned only re: a call in warranty, no lodging/letting issue.
Lease of a lot for a horse stable, dispute over pavement removal and unauthorized subletting; no dwelling/lodging facts.
Vendor's privilege on house-furnishing goods sold on credit; no letting/lodging arrangement at issue.

holding_summary: Defendant leased his house to plaintiff for one month at $20/month with half paid in advance, then re-let and delivered possession to a second tenant before the first month expired; the court enforced the one-month letting as a completed contract and awarded the first lessee damages for the lessor's breach.

quotes.text: Where the proof shows that a house has been leased for one month at a fixed price, and one-half of the amount paid in advanoe, and the lessor leases the house to another party, and puts him in possession before the end of the month, the Court will award such damages to the first lessee as the proof shows that he has sustained by the violation of the lease by the lessor.

notes: A one-month house letting for pay, treated by the court as an ordinary enforceable lease contract entitling the disappointed lessee to damages -- letting as an ordinary incident of ownership.
Succession administration/sequestration jurisdiction dispute over crop proceeds; no dwelling-letting issue.
